days.theme: Yuzhong peninsula on foot — monument, 250 m skywalk, confluence, then Hongya Cave once the lights come on
days.why: Train clears ~11:20, hotel is at Jiefangbei, so the whole day stays inside one walkable peninsula and never needs a second metro hop. Jiefangbei is literally at the door — do it while bags are being dropped. Raffles Crystal deck (10:00–21:00, book ahead) is deliberately parked in the 15:00–16:30 slot: late-August Chongqing is 38 °C+ and this is a ticketed, air-conditioned lift-and-glass-deck block that also gives you the aerial read of the confluence you are about to walk. Chaotianmen Docks sits directly under Raffles, so it is a free ten-minute transition, and it lets you eyeball tomorrow's night-cruise pier in daylight. Evening is sequenced against the actual light-up: research confirms Hongya Cave lights come on around 20:00 in summer (not 19:00) and run to 23:00, and it thins out noticeably after 21:00. So Kuixinglou Plaza takes the pre-dinner dusk slot (~18:30) — it is a 30-minute walk-in-at-street-level-onto-the-22nd-floor trick, the single best demonstration of Chongqing's verticality and 400 m from the hotel — then dinner, then Qiansimen Bridge (~20:15) for the head-on framed shot, then Hongya Cave itself from ~21:00 for the full 105 minutes through eleven levels with the crush already easing. Only three evening pieces, one of which is the destination; Jiangbei riverbank is cut to ideas because it is the same subject from a near-identical angle 130 m away.
days.load_note: 360 min stop time (6.0 h) across a ~11:20–23:00 window — correct for an arrival day with two meals and a check-in in it.

days.theme: West end in the morning, cross the Yangtze by cable car mid-afternoon, south-bank lanes at dusk, both rivers by boat at night
days.why: One clean west-to-east-to-south sweep with no backtracking, which matters more here than raw distance — Chongqing's coordinates lie, everything is stairs, ramps and lift shafts. Morning is the Eling cluster: Liziba monorail first at ~09:00 (30 min, trains every 5–10 min, shoot from the platform across the road), then straight uphill to Eling Park for the Liangjiang Pavilion two-rivers panorama before the afternoon haze, then Testbed 2 — which is the old Eling printing works immediately adjacent, not a separate trip — and lunch inside its cafés. Afternoon crosses east: Baixiang Ju by metro to Xiaoshizi, then the Yangtze Cableway is used as actual transport rather than a detour, carrying you north→south straight to Longmenhao Old Street, which sits at the south station. Longmenhao then takes the dusk slot it wants (~17:00–18:15, golden light on the terraced hillside) with dinner following on the same street. The night belongs to one thing only: the Two Rivers night cruise, boarding Chaotianmen ~19:45 for a 20:00 sailing (departures run roughly 19:00–22:00, about every half hour, ~45 min afloat plus boarding). Deliberately NOT stacking the cableway into the evening as a second night viewpoint — the queues after dark are the worst of the day and a blown queue would cost you the boat.
days.load_note: 450 min stop time (7.5 h) — sits inside the 8–10 h ceiling on purpose, because vertical transfers and August heat eat the difference.

days.theme: Departure only — 08:00 train from Chongqing North, nothing else is real
days.why: An 08:00 departure with a 60-minute station buffer means leaving the hotel around 06:45 and being awake at 06:00. There is no sight in Chongqing worth attempting in that window, and attempting one risks the train. Breakfast at the hotel, go. Everything that would have lived here has been absorbed into days 1 and 2.
days.load_note: 0 min stop time — day intentionally empty.

ideas.name: Jiangbei riverbank
ideas.why: Cut purely to avoid four night viewpoints in one evening. It is the wide across-the-river panorama of Hongya Cave with reflections — genuinely lovely, but it is the same subject as Qiansimen Bridge from a whisker away, and Qiansimen wins because it is on the direct walking line between dinner and Hongya Cave with zero detour. Pick this up instead of the bridge if you want reflections over the head-on framing, or add it after Hongya Cave on day 1 if you still have legs at 22:45.

ideas.name: Chongqing West (alt station)
ideas.why: Not a sight — it is the contingency departure station, 40–60 min from Jiefangbei in morning traffic versus roughly 30 for Chongqing North. Only relevant if the day-3 ticket turns out to leave from West rather than North, in which case the 06:45 hotel departure has to become 06:00. Confirm which station the ticket is for before booking anything else on day 3.

ideas.name: Check in at KS Kongshang
ideas.why: Not a sight — logistics, kept out of the stop list per the no-hotels rule. Practically: the hotel is on the 52nd floor of the Xinhua International Building at Jiefangbei, formal check-in is after 14:00, so on arrival day drop bags around 12:15, eat, and collect the room later in the afternoon. Passport needed at the desk.

notes: Yangtze Cableway is the one hard booking risk of the trip. Tickets are same-day only, released from 07:45 on the 重庆索道公司 WeChat mini-program at the official ¥30, and they routinely sell out 2–3 hours ahead — arriving at the station at 15:00 can mean a 20:00 slot. Buy the day-2 slot at 07:45 that morning, before leaving for Liziba. Xinhua Road (north) station is far busier than Shangxin Street (south); if the only slots left are late, swap the order and do Baixiang Ju after the crossing.

Hongya Cave light-up is ~20:00 in summer, not the 19:00 the current notes assume, and runs to ~23:00. Shops trade 10:00–23:00. The 19:30–22:00 window is peak crush; after 21:00 is materially calmer, which is why day 1 places it there.

Two Rivers night cruise: departures roughly 19:00–22:00 from Chaotianmen, about every 30 minutes on a fill-and-go basis, some schedules run fixed 19:20 / 20:40 shifts during maintenance periods. Sailing is ~45 min, so 75 min door-to-door is right. Book ahead and reconfirm the pier — day 1 walks you past Chaotianmen Docks precisely so you can verify it in daylight.
Raffles Crystal deck is 10:00–21:00 and needs booking. Treat the 15:00 slot as heat management as much as sightseeing.

Coordinate distances across Yuzhong understate real travel badly — Baixiang Ju to the cableway north station reads as a few hundred metres and is a stair-and-lift maze. Both full days are built to stay inside one cluster at a time for exactly this reason.

Arrival (11:00) and departure (08:00) times are both flagged provisional. Day 1 has slack — a two-hour late arrival only costs Jiefangbei. Day 3 has none; if the departure moves earlier, nothing changes because the day is already empty.
Late August is peak heat and humidity. The plan front-loads outdoor climbing (Eling, Liziba) into the morning and puts the ticketed indoor block in the afternoon on both days.
